testPolicy.text: Duke University is test-optional for both first-year and transfer applicants in the 2026-2027 admissions cycle. Students who apply without SAT or ACT scores will not be at a disadvantage. Self-reported scores are accepted; official scores are required only from students who enroll.

Published total range: 103,180 to 103,975.

aidPromise.text: Duke meets 100% of demonstrated need for undergraduates (aid offers will most likely include a loan, work-study and grant). Initiative for Students from the Carolinas: full tuition grants for admitted North Carolina and South Carolina residents with total family income of $150,000 or less; at $65,000 or less, full tuition plus help with housing, meals and some course materials, without student loans.

facts.text: Students from North Carolina and South Carolina with family income of $150,000 or less get full-tuition grants; at $65,000 or less Duke also covers housing and meals without loans.
Duke says 21% of its last first-year class attended tuition-free.
For fall 2025, 2,910 of 55,541 applicants were admitted (about 5.2%) and 1,749 enrolled.
The 2026-27 first-year cost of attendance is $103,180 to $103,975 before aid, with billed charges of $98,788 (Pratt engineering students pay $60 more in dues).
Duke has one binding Early Decision round (November 2) and Regular Decision (January 4); no Early Action.
Alumni interviews are optional and offered only to some applicants; not being offered one does not affect the chances of admission.
